name: Amaziah
bio:
Amaziah succeeded his father Joash as king of Judah after Joash was assassinated by two of his own servants and buried with his ancestors in the City of David (2 Kings 12:20-21).

## 📖 Core Story: Victory Over Edom, Defeat by Israel

Amaziah reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, doing right in the LORD's eyes but not like David, following his father Joash's example; the high places remained. Once his throne was secure, he executed the servants who had killed his father, but spared their children, following the law of Moses that forbade punishing children for their parents' sins. He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and captured Sela, renaming it Joktheel (2 Kings 14:1-7).

Flush with that victory, Amaziah challenged Jehoash, king of Israel, to battle. Jehoash warned him off with a parable about a thistle provoking a cedar, but Amaziah wouldn't listen, and the two met at Beth Shemesh, where Judah was routed. Jehoash captured Amaziah, broke down part of Jerusalem's wall, and plundered the temple and palace treasuries before returning to Samaria (2 Kings 14:8-14). Amaziah lived fifteen more years after Jehoash's death, but was eventually assassinated by conspirators in Jerusalem; he fled to Lachish, where they caught and killed him anyway. He was buried in the City of David, and the people made his son Azariah king in his place (2 Kings 14:17-21).
